claims.text: The initial intermediate layer is a homogeneous, single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Composition modification followed by controlled heat treatment will induce coherent tungsten-rich nano-precipitates in the alloy matrix.
Coherent tungsten-rich nano-precipitates will enhance thermal transport pathways.
Tungsten-rich nano-precipitates will reinforce the alloy's grain boundaries.
The tungsten-rich nano-precipitates provide additional electron-conduction paths.
The tungsten-rich nano-precipitates provide additional phonon-conduction paths.
The additional electron and phonon conduction paths improve thermal conductivity.
Coherent precipitate interfaces mitigate crack propagation.
Mitigation of crack propagation preserves mechanical strength under operational conditions.
The modified alloy will exhibit a statistically significant increase in thermal conductivity relative to the homogeneous-alloy baseline.
The modified alloy will maintain its mechanical properties within acceptable performance limits.
The proposed benefits will persist during thermal cycling at approximately 800–1000°C and under mechanical loading representative of plasma disruptions.
The benefits depend on maintaining a controlled precipitate volume fraction.
Excessive precipitate content may cause phase instability or embrittlement.
Temperatures above approximately 1000°C may cause phase instability or embrittlement.
